title: How Crypto Millionaires Lost Their Fortune
summary: Recounts the 2022 crypto crash and anonymous first-hand stories of traders who lost fortunes and went into debt, arguing for diversified funds instead.

assertions.quote: I kept trading and losing and now I have nothing left I still have the debt

verdicts.note: eToro retail investors do not rebalance out of crypto after price rises or falls, even in the top return quintile, and kept the same hold-through strategy after Bitcoin's 65% crash in early 2018; documents the not-taking-profits behaviour, not the resulting P&L.

assertions.quote: I enrolled in a BS master's program to get ten thousand dollars of student loans per semester for more trading capital

verdicts.note: Margin and leverage mean losses can exceed deposited capital; brokers and regulators document negative balances and margin calls.
At high leverage investors risk losing all or more than their initial margin, especially in gapping markets, which is why ESMA imposed negative balance protection on retail CFD accounts.

The FCA warns that margin close-out is not a guaranteed stop-loss, so in volatile markets leveraged CFD clients could lose their entire deposit or sustain losses exceeding it, leaving them owing money to the firm.

assertions.quote: when the value of a cryptocurrency is pretty much completely based on whether or not people believe it's worth anything

verdicts.note: Retail entry is driven by the Bitcoin price itself (safe-haven, distrust and macro explanations fall short) and a panel VAR shows a one-s.d. jump in app users lifts the Bitcoin price by about 6 points within a month, supporting a speculative feedback loop; the paper describes the system as self-referential but does not directly test cash-flow fundamentals.

Retail traders hold crypto momentum-style while trading stocks and gold contrarian, and the authors conjecture that with few fundamentals investors read price moves as signals of future adoption, creating amplification; evidence is about investor beliefs rather than what sets prices.

assertions.quote: you should really stick to acting instead of investing advice

verdicts.note: Celebrity-promoted tokens have repeatedly collapsed and regulators have fined undisclosed paid promotions.

Nudge marketed through TV real-estate celebrities promising a 'proven' formula, yet a survey in the FTC's filings found over 95% of seminar attendees paid Nudge more than they netted from real estate; Zurixx likewise used celebrity endorsements with false earnings claims.

assertions.quote: actual wealthy people invest consistently in mutual funds and index funds in their 401ks and their IRAs month after month year after year
more than 80 000 Bitcoin investors had their millionaire status revoked due to this crypto market crash

verdicts.note: BIS research found the majority of retail crypto app users who bought between 2015 and 2022 likely lost money because most entered near peaks.

Across 95 countries 73% of crypto-exchange app users first downloaded when Bitcoin was above $20,000 (its Oct 2022 price), and a $100-a-month simulation from first download puts 75-81% of users underwater with a median loss of 48%; returns are simulated from entry timing, not observed account P&L.

On eToro crypto reached over 85% of dollars invested at the end-2017 price peak, Bitcoin then fell about 65% in Jan-Feb 2018 and investors did not rebalance out, which implies boom entrants sat through the crash, though the paper never measures realized profit or loss.
